_sobre: Relatos de bug (estilo issue do GitHub) para as instâncias SWT-Bench. Descrevem só o sintoma observado, sem indicar a correção. A chave 'repro' é conferida por preparar.py: precisa dar resultado diferente na versão com defeito e na corrigida.

apnumber__d1_zero_excluido.title: apnumber(0) is not spelled out
apnumber__d1_zero_excluido.body:
The docs say numbers from 0 to 9 are returned as words, but zero comes back as a digit string.

```python
>>> from alvo import apnumber
>>> apnumber(0)
'0'
```

Expected `'zero'`. Other single digits (e.g. `apnumber(5)` -> `'five'`) work fine.

apnumber__d2_nove_excluido.title: apnumber(9) returns '9' instead of 'nine'
apnumber__d2_nove_excluido.body:
Single-digit numbers should be spelled out, but 9 is returned as a digit.

```python
>>> from alvo import apnumber
>>> apnumber(9)
'9'
```

Expected `'nine'`.

apnumber__d3_except_incompleto.title: apnumber(None) crashes with TypeError
apnumber__d3_except_incompleto.body:
Values that cannot be converted to int are supposed to be returned unchanged as a string (`str(value)`), but passing `None` raises:

```python
>>> from alvo import apnumber
>>> apnumber(None)
Traceback (most recent call last):
  ...
TypeError: int() argument must be a string, a bytes-like object or a real number, not 'NoneType'
```

Expected `'None'`, the same way `apnumber('abc')` returns `'abc'`.

cpf_validate__d1_aceita_zero.title: validate() accepts the all-zeros CPF
cpf_validate__d1_aceita_zero.body:
A CPF made only of zeros is not a valid number and should be rejected with `InvalidFormat`, but it is accepted:

```python
>>> from alvo import validate
>>> validate('00000000000')
'00000000000'
```

Expected: `InvalidFormat` is raised.

cpf_validate__d2_comprimento_minimo.title: CPF with too many digits raises InvalidChecksum instead of InvalidLength
cpf_validate__d2_comprimento_minimo.body:
Any CPF whose compacted form does not have exactly 11 digits should raise `InvalidLength`. With 12 digits we get the wrong exception:

```python
>>> from alvo import validate
>>> validate('111444777350')
Traceback (most recent call last):
  ...
alvo.InvalidChecksum
```

Expected: `InvalidLength`.

cpf_validate__d3_nao_remove_ponto.title: Formatted CPF with dots is rejected
cpf_validate__d3_nao_remove_ponto.body:
`validate()` is documented to accept CPFs in the usual `XXX.XXX.XXX-XX` format (spaces, dots and hyphens are removed before validating), but a correctly formatted valid CPF fails:

```python
>>> from alvo import validate
>>> validate('111.444.777-35')
Traceback (most recent call last):
  ...
alvo.InvalidFormat
```

Expected: returns the compact form `'11144477735'`.

cpf_validate__d4_segundo_digito.title: Valid CPF rejected with InvalidChecksum
cpf_validate__d4_segundo_digito.body:
Some perfectly valid CPF numbers are rejected as having a wrong check digit:

```python
>>> from alvo import validate
>>> validate('11144477735')
Traceback (most recent call last):
  ...
alvo.InvalidChecksum
```

`111.444.777-35` is a well-known valid CPF (both check digits are correct). Expected: returns `'11144477735'`.

intword__d1_mil_sem_sufixo.title: intword(1000) is not humanized
intword__d1_mil_sem_sufixo.body:
Numbers of one thousand or more should be written with a word suffix, but exactly 1000 comes back unchanged:

```python
>>> from alvo import intword
>>> intword(1000)
'1000'
```

Expected `'1.0 thousand'`.

intword__d2_sem_carry.title: intword(999999) returns '1000.0 thousand'
intword__d2_sem_carry.body:
When rounding pushes a value up to the next power, the suffix is not promoted:

```python
>>> from alvo import intword
>>> intword(999999)
'1000.0 thousand'
```

Expected `'1.0 million'`.

intword__d3_perde_sinal.title: intword drops the minus sign of negative numbers
intword__d3_perde_sinal.body:
Negative values lose their sign:

```python
>>> from alvo import intword
>>> intword(-1000000)
'1.0 million'
```

Expected `'-1.0 million'`.

intword__d4_bisect_left.title: intword(10**100) does not return '1.0 googol'
intword__d4_bisect_left.body:
A googol should be humanized as `'1.0 googol'`, but we get a huge number with the previous suffix:

```python
>>> from alvo import intword
>>> intword(10**100)
'9999999999999999827367757839185598317239782875580932278577147150336.0 decillion'
```

Expected `'1.0 googol'`.

luhn_validate__d1_posicoes_trocadas.title: Valid Luhn number rejected
luhn_validate__d1_posicoes_trocadas.body:
The textbook Luhn example number is rejected:

```python
>>> from alvo import validate
>>> validate('79927398713')
Traceback (most recent call last):
  ...
alvo.InvalidChecksum
```

`79927398713` has a valid Luhn check digit. Expected: returns `'79927398713'`.

luhn_validate__d2_sem_vai_um.title: Luhn validation fails for numbers with digits >= 5 in doubled positions
luhn_validate__d2_sem_vai_um.body:
Valid numbers are rejected when some of the doubled digits are 5 or more:

```python
>>> from alvo import validate
>>> validate('79927398713')
Traceback (most recent call last):
  ...
alvo.InvalidChecksum
```

`79927398713` is the standard valid Luhn example. Expected: returns `'79927398713'`.

luhn_validate__d3_aceita_vazio.title: validate('') accepts an empty string
luhn_validate__d3_aceita_vazio.body:
An empty value should be rejected with `InvalidFormat`, but it is accepted:

```python
>>> from alvo import validate
>>> validate('')
''
```

Expected: `InvalidFormat` is raised.

luhn_validate__d4_converte_str.title: validate() returns a string when given an int
luhn_validate__d4_converte_str.body:
`validate()` should return the value it received, unchanged, when it is valid. When an int is passed, a str comes back:

```python
>>> from alvo import validate
>>> validate(79927398713)
'79927398713'
```

Expected the int `79927398713`.

naturalsize__d1_base_inclusiva.title: naturalsize(1000) returns '1000 Bytes'
naturalsize__d1_base_inclusiva.body:
Exactly one kilobyte is not converted to the next unit:

```python
>>> from alvo import naturalsize
>>> naturalsize(1000)
'1000 Bytes'
```

Expected `'1.0 kB'`.

naturalsize__d2_base_binaria.title: naturalsize(binary=True) gives wrong values
naturalsize__d2_base_binaria.body:
With `binary=True` the result should use powers of 1024 (KiB, MiB...), but the numbers look like they are computed with powers of 1000:

```python
>>> from alvo import naturalsize
>>> naturalsize(3000000, binary=True)
'3.0 MiB'
```

3000000 / 1024**2 = 2.86..., so expected `'2.9 MiB'`.

naturalsize__d3_singular_sem_abs.title: naturalsize(-1) uses the plural 'Bytes'
naturalsize__d3_singular_sem_abs.body:
`naturalsize(1)` correctly returns `'1 Byte'`, but the negative counterpart uses the plural:

```python
>>> from alvo import naturalsize
>>> naturalsize(-1)
'-1 Bytes'
```

Expected `'-1 Byte'`.

naturalsize__d4_sem_subir_sufixo.title: naturalsize(999999) returns '1000.0 kB'
naturalsize__d4_sem_subir_sufixo.body:
When formatting rounds a value up to the size of the next unit, the unit is not promoted:

```python
>>> from alvo import naturalsize
>>> naturalsize(999999)
'1000.0 kB'
```

Expected `'1.0 MB'`.

ordinal__d1_treze_esquecido.title: ordinal(13) returns '13rd'
ordinal__d1_treze_esquecido.body:
```python
>>> from alvo import ordinal
>>> ordinal(13)
'13rd'
```

Expected `'13th'` (11, 12 and 13 always take 'th').

ordinal__d2_modulo_errado.title: ordinal(11) returns '11st'
ordinal__d2_modulo_errado.body:
```python
>>> from alvo import ordinal
>>> ordinal(11)
'11st'
```

Expected `'11th'`.

ordinal__d3_ignora_centena.title: ordinal(111) returns '111st'
ordinal__d3_ignora_centena.body:
Small numbers like 11 work, but larger numbers ending in 11/12/13 get the wrong suffix:

```python
>>> from alvo import ordinal
>>> ordinal(111)
'111st'
```

Expected `'111th'`.

ordinal__d4_retorno_vazio.title: ordinal() returns an empty string for non-numeric input
ordinal__d4_retorno_vazio.body:
Values that cannot be converted to int should be returned as `str(value)`, but an empty string comes back:

```python
>>> from alvo import ordinal
>>> ordinal('something else')
''
```

Expected `'something else'`.
